correctness.rationale: Theorem 1 verified by independent recomputation: f(x)=x^6+3x^4-5x^2+7 satisfies f(even)=3 mod 4, f(odd)=2 mod 4, while squares mod 4 are {0,1}; disjoint, so no integer solutions. Mod-8 strengthening f(Z)={3,6,7} vs QR {0,1,4} also recomputed and disjoint, giving C(Z_2)=empty. Discriminant independently recomputed via sympy as -4714544128 (matches Bareiss claim, nonzero, so affine model smooth). Theorem 2 verified: N(a,b)/b^6 square in Q iff N(a,b) square in Q (b^6=(b^3)^2), and integer square in Q is square in Z (lowest-terms forces denominator 1). All three residue cases recomputed: b odd/a even -> 3 mod 4; both odd -> 2 mod 4; v2(b)=1/a odd -> 5 mod 8 (using b^2=4 mod 8, b^4=b^6=0 mod 8, odd squares 1 mod 8). Exhaustive mod-8 scan over all (a,b) with not-both-even and b not 0 mod 4 confirms every 4-ndivides-b class obstructed; independent recheck found zero unobstructed classes. All three stdlib verifiers print VERIFY_OK. Projective-closure remark (two Q-points at infinity, smoothness via dF/dY=+-2) checked correct. No QC machinery claimed; limitations stated honestly. No essential inference or boundary condition fails.
